VIKI Agent / Guide

21 min read · 12 sections

How VIKI Agent works

VIKI Agent is a local workspace for proactive coding with Claude Code and the knowledge you keep in Markdown. It brings the next action, the agent's work and the evidence for your review into one place.

You can move from a note or a due task to a conversation, work in a code folder, inspect the result and keep a useful finding for later.

Start with Getting started for installation and a first conversation. See Known issues for limits you may run into.

01The parts and the value they provide

VIKI Agent's parts form a workflow rather than one automatic authority.

PartWhat it doesWhy it helps
DecisionEvaluates supported signals with a model, current context, history and local gates; falls back to rulesCan raise a suggestion or start eligible work within your grants
Claude Code, run by VIKI AgentRuns Anthropic's unmodified claude executable for each chat and presents its conversation, tools, questions, permissions and statusKeeps execution visible alongside the work it concerns
Code workspaceConnects a trusted folder to chat, file inspection and the supported review toolsLets you inspect a change in its project context
Markdown vaultHolds notes you can read, link, search and attach as explicit excerptsKeeps decisions and source material in files you can use outside the app
Review and recovery controlsBind supported actions to the version you reviewed and preserve recoverable stateHelp you notice changed inputs and recover interrupted work

The workflow runs like this:

Decision chooses attention, timing and eligible work. Claude Code does the work you start or allow through a grant. A permission, a draft proposal and a completed file change each have their own meaning.

02How profiles, Bots and routines fit together

A profile, a Bot and a routine describe different ways to use the agent runtime, which Claude Code supplies. VIKI Agent supplies the interface and the surrounding controls: workspace selection, chat state, routines, proactive checks and review.

PartWhat it holds or decidesExample
ProfileSaved role instructions and launch configurationResearch's instructions, model and tools
BotA profile and persistent vault pair, its reopenable conversation and the routines using that pairResearch in your product vault
Chat/sessionOne Claude Code conversation, whether you opened it directly, through a Bot or for a runA follow-up about the research brief
RoutineA prompt, profile, workspace, trigger and run settings; each attempt gets a fresh chatPick up Research's oldest todo card
Native subagentA helper called from a chat for one taskThe Kanban pack's Checker checks the card's Done when list
VaultMarkdown project overviews, tasks, cards, sources and results10-projects/website/website.md and kanban/backup-comparison.md
DecisionObserves supported signals, evaluates attention and checks which work may startOffer Start for Research or begin its eligible routine
JEVTypeSafe's optional assessment model within Decision; the app shows it as the Decision modelRate whether a due task advances a listed goal and whether preparation would help

Where things are kept:

  • VIKI's local app data
    profiles, Bot conversation links, routines and Decision records. JEV's assessments are Decision records, not new vault notes.
  • Claude Code
    owns the original chat transcripts.
  • The vault
    goals, cards and saved results, as Markdown files. A reply becomes a note when you or a chat writes it there.

See Conversations and local state for storage and recovery details.

Chief routes requests

Chief is a Bot conversation for routing requests. With the Kanban pack, it records a request as a card for a specialist.

  • VIKI's local Kanban and routine checks
    can then start that specialist through Start Bots' work. JEV is not required for that start.
  • A fixed-time routine
    uses the scheduler instead.

Both paths produce a new run chat, separate from the Bot's regular conversation. See Chat, Chief or a specialist for the entry points and a worked example.

JEV's part in Decision

  • JEV
    receives the state VIKI permits it to see and returns probabilities, scores and choices. It neither edits the vault nor sends a message to Chief.
  • VIKI
    converts those assessments into local attention and work decisions.
  • Claude Code
    performs any resulting chat work under its own permissions.

The Decision guide explains JEV's inputs, outputs and rules fallback, and where goals come from.

04The proactive loop

Decision connects opportunities, attention, delegated work and feedback. This makes proactivity useful between prompts: a supported next step can reach you, and an eligible task can start within the authority you have chosen.

StageWhat it doesYour control
NoticeGathers supported signals such as due tasks, approvals, runs, inbox activity, Kanban cards, vault health, code folders, repeated workflows and knowledge-upkeep opportunitiesChoose the workspace, what VIKI watches, sharing settings and exclusions; enable or pause proactivity
DecideWeighs relevance, novelty, actionability, current context, timing, attention cost and authorityReview why an item appeared, defer it, mark it Not useful or stop that topic
ProposeOffers the proposals listed belowInspect the source and choose whether to send the prepared draft
WorkStarts the kinds of work listed belowAsk first, Allowed or Off govern each kind of start; Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage and the vault's policy can hold them; Claude Code's own permissions still apply
LearnUses engagement and feedback to adapt local Decision scoring and attention estimatesInspect Learning, compare Start / Now / Based on, disable learning or reset it

The Propose stage offers:

  • reusable skills;
  • use of one of your own skills;
  • a captured source worth a literature note;
  • retrospectives;
  • question tuning and supported note upkeep;
  • a handoff for a nearly full chat;
  • literature notes for fetched pages.

The Work stage starts these, with the required grant and activity limits:

  • a chat for an eligible due task;
  • a Bot's tested routine when one of your cards waits for its seat;
  • plan-mode looks at trusted code folders' day-old changes;
  • plan-mode second looks at the chat you have open;
  • plan-mode plans for stalled projects and overdue tasks;
  • the inbox's read-only suggestion run when the inbox piles up;
  • a trusted code folder's saved checks on a new commit.

The loop requires:

  • proactivity to be enabled and unpaused;
  • the app to be running;
  • a window to be open.

Proactivity starts disabled. Once it is on, the defaults are:

  • Ask first
    Start chats to do work, Start Bots' work and Run my saved checks.
  • Allowed
    Prepare drafts, the plan-mode looks, second looks and project plans, and the inbox's read-only suggestion run. VIKI can begin those without a click.

Each plan-mode chat waits for your approval before it changes anything. Improvement offers remain reviewed drafts even when Start chats to do work is Allowed. Only the kinds of work listed above are proposed or started.

The Decision guide lists every grant with its default and daily limit.

Learning from earlier responses

  • Opening or acting on an item
    provides positive engagement.
  • Not useful
    provides negative feedback.
  • Not now
    defers an item without supplying a positive or negative fitting label.

Recent feedback also supplies bounded context for later Decision requests.

With Learning on, VIKI updates its local numbers every five minutes. Later decisions use the learned numbers while learning is enabled.

  • Scoring weights and topic offsets
    need at least 20 eligible labelled model decisions, including three positive and three negative labels.
  • Attention reach and interruption-cost estimates
    can adapt before that fitting threshold.

This is local preference calibration. It does not train Claude or the optional Decision service's underlying model, and it does not guarantee better outcomes on every decision.

In the demonstration, the Learning screen shows sample numbers: across 20 sample decisions, the goal-link weight moves from 0.600 to 1.266. They are sample data, not anyone's real results. A single Not useful click does not refit the weights at once.

Learning can be turned off or reset. A reset:

  • removes the learned snapshot and starts its learning window again;
  • preserves recorded decisions and labels.

Changes to reusable skills, knowledge and question wording follow review workflows rather than automatic self-modification.

Decision and Claude Code use separate model connections:

  • Decision
    uses a separate model service and sharing controls, with a rules fallback. You can pick the model version; you can't switch to another provider.
  • Claude Code
    uses its own provider connection.

The demonstration in the guide shows both at work.

05Proactive attention: Decision

Open Decision in the left rail to set up the proactive loop:

  • Proactive VIKI
    enables the loop.
  • Decision model
    saves its key and selects a version.
  • What leaves this computer
    controls titles, short excerpts or sections and the folders or tags to exclude.

What Decision observes

Supported observations include:

  • due tasks, approvals, agent runs, inbox activity, routines and Kanban cards;
  • bounded vault changes, stopped saves and deleted notes about to expire;
  • memories whose cited notes changed;
  • chats waiting for you and messages that may not have reached Claude Code;
  • MCP servers filling a chat's context and stopped messaging bridges;
  • code folders with changes left uncommitted for a day;
  • code folders at a new commit their saved checks have not run on;
  • inbox captures with no suggested destination;
  • replies in the chat you have open that finish a long task or corrected work;
  • active projects with no change for two weeks and tasks three days or more overdue;
  • the context share of the chat you have open and the web pages its last reply fetched.

The model receives the permitted context, goals and recent feedback. Its answers inform whether to stay quiet, add an item to the list, show a badge, nudge or alert, and when to surface it.

Local checks also apply:

  • Local gates
    apply quiet hours, focus, typing, muted topics, activity limits and your grants.
  • Without a usable model answer
    the local rules still surface supported items.
  • Bot routine eligibility and scheduled starts
    have their own local checks, as described above.

Grants for drafts and starts

What VIKI may do separates Prepare drafts from Start chats to do work, each with Off, Ask first and Allowed. The settings work like this:

  • Start chats to do work
    an eligible due task with Allowed authority can start a chat without another prompt.
  • Look on my behalf
    lets VIKI start a plan-mode chat in a trusted code folder whose uncommitted changes have sat for a day or more.
  • Take a second look at my work
    lets VIKI start a plan-mode chat that reads the notes a long or corrected reply edited and proposes one finding as a plan.
  • Plan next steps for my projects
    lets VIKI start a plan-mode chat that proposes three next actions for a stalled project, or ticks and new dates for overdue tasks.
  • Prepare drafts
    also lets VIKI offer a message for the chat you have open, a handoff when its context is nearly full or literature notes for pages its last reply fetched. It waits in the message box for you to send.
  • Run my saved checks
    lets VIKI run the saved checks you have run in a trusted code folder when it moves to a new commit.
  • Suggest destinations for my inbox
    lets VIKI run the inbox's read-only suggestion run on its own, so suggestions wait in the triage.
  • Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage
    holds the chats, Bot runs and inbox suggestion runs VIKI would start on its own while your plan use reaches the share you pick or your plan limit is reached. It does not hold saved checks, message drafts or your own starts.

These rules also apply:

  • Vault policy
    in a protected vault VIKI starts only plans, and in a read-only vault none.
  • Chats at once
    at most two chats that Decision starts run at once, within separate daily limits.
  • Tool use
    Claude Code's own permissions still govern tool use.
  • Improvement offers and vault upkeep
    retain their draft and approval paths.

Where the loop reaches you

The loop reaches you inside the app.

  • It does not choose among your devices or escalate to a messaging bridge after silence.
  • It starts a Bot only through that Bot's tested routine set to Only when a card is waiting, under Start Bots' work.
  • Messaging connections and Bot routine notices have separate controls.

See the Decision guide.

Decision and Approvals have different jobs

  • The Decision page concerns what VIKI chooses to show, hold back or begin.
  • The Approvals view concerns proposals and choices you review: tool requests, plans and questions, note proposals for a protected vault, skill proposals, vault-upkeep proposals and proposed question wording.

What each review records:

  • Edit to a protected vault
    VIKI Agent keeps the proposal itself. Handing it to a chat does not establish that it has been applied.
  • Skill approval
    also records your intent rather than installing a skill.

Re-read the resulting source before treating a proposed change as completed. See Needs you and Approvals for the review surfaces and Skills and memory for creating skill proposals.

06Claude Code: execution you can inspect

VIKI Agent runs Anthropic's unmodified claude executable for each chat session. That Claude Code process uses your instructions, skills, hooks and permission configuration. The app presents its messages, tool activity, questions, hook notices and agent runs in the desktop interface.

Where Claude Code's model requests go depends on the connection:

  • Claude Code sign-in
    the sign-in your Claude Code is set up with: your Claude plan, an API key or a cloud provider. To keep chats on your Claude subscription only, turn off Let Claude Code use its other sign-in methods in Settings › Chat.
  • Your own model
    set up in Settings → Providers, it instead sends Claude Code's model requests through VIKI's local gateway to the endpoint you choose. Claude Code still runs the tools.

Offline inference requires a local model server. Optional integrations and the commands you run have their own network behavior.

Permission modes keep their Claude Code meaning. When Claude Code asks for a tool permission, the card offers Allow once or Deny. Some configured modes and existing rules allow tools without a card.

Warning

A code folder, a worktree or a preview is not a sandbox: commands run with your rights.

See Needs you and Approvals and Security.

07Integrity has separate layers

Integrity depends on the path a change takes. Keep these layers distinct when setting up a vault or reviewing an agent's work.

LayerWhat protects itWhat you still review
Claude Code executionYour instructions, hooks, permissions and the app's visible controlsWhether the configured rules cover the operation and whether the result is correct
Saving a note in the appSaves go only to an ordinary vault, and a save stops if the note changed elsewhere firstThe intended content, the destination and any conflict or Recovery notice
Governed proposals and memoryA choice or approval bound to the content reviewed; protected changes remain proposalsWhether the source still supports the claim and whether the change was actually made

Hooks belong to your Claude Code configuration

A hook can check an operation at a point supported by Claude Code.

  • VIKI Agent
    preserves that configuration and displays blocked or failing hook notices it receives. It does not supply a universal guard around every command or tool.
  • The starter vault
    includes deny rules, but ships no guard hook.

Adding an integrity hook requires choosing its checks and understanding which operations it covers.

VIKI Agent's own note saves have their own checks, separate from your hooks:

  • Do not assume that a Claude Code hook validates a save made by the app.
  • Conversely, a save only stops when the note changed elsewhere first. It does not inspect the meaning of a change Claude Code makes.

Security explains these boundaries.

Vault policy determines what the app can save

An ordinary vault is one whose policy is Ordinary; it is the only kind VIKI Agent saves notes into. There, VIKI Agent can save a single note and run the documented rename, move, archive, delete-to-recovery and restore actions:

  • on Windows;
  • on APFS on macOS;
  • on ext4, XFS, Btrfs or tmpfs on Linux.

If the note changed elsewhere first, a save stops and your draft stays. The app also supports a create-only copy, under attachments/, of a chat attachment you choose to keep.

The other cases:

  • Protected vault
    VIKI Agent does not save into a protected vault. An edit there becomes a proposal for you to hand to Claude Code.
  • Read-only vault
    does not become writable because a note declares a title, tag or status.
  • Other filesystems
    a vault stays read-only for VIKI Agent's own note saves and actions.
  • New vaults and backups
    creating a new vault and restoring a backup into a new, read-only folder are separate supported paths.

See The Vault view and Sessions and data.

08Keep context from aging

Old context can fail in different ways:

  • a file can change after you attach it;
  • an approval can refer to earlier text;
  • a long conversation can lose detail;
  • a source can become inaccurate even while its bytes remain unchanged.

VIKI Agent provides controls for the first kinds of staleness. Source accuracy still needs your judgment.

What VIKI Agent checks

SituationSafeguardYour next step
Selected note text changes after you attach an excerptThe selected lines are read again before sending; changed excerpt text is refusedOpen the current note and attach the relevant passage again
A proposal changes after reviewChoices name the reviewed revision; changed content can make them staleRead the updated item before deciding again
An approved memory record changesIts local approval applies to the exact bytes; changed bytes need review againInspect the claim and its sources before approving it
A memory is superseded or wrongSupported memory actions can correct or retire it, within the platform and vault policyKeep the replacement precise and review the old record's retirement
A conversation growsContext & loadout shows the last reported usage and compaction information from Claude Code; an earlier report can remain visible after a later read failsRevisit the goal, inspect the current files and choose the context needed for the next step
A source is old but unchangedA content hash does not detect a factual change in the worldCheck the source, record a correction and review dependent decisions

Memory review is explicit:

  • Approval
    a record that says status: approved does not authorize itself. The device must have approved that exact content. An inference does not become active solely because the file calls it approved.
  • Another device
    moving records to another device does not transfer local approval.
  • Active confirms approval of this version.
    It does not confirm that its cited sources are still current: an unchanged memory can remain Active after a source changes.
  • Excerpts
    excerpt freshness checks cover the selected passage. Retiring a memory can leave a claim-only excerpt unchanged.

Review the record's current status before reusing its claim.

Note

The memory service does not automatically retrieve records into each prompt, expire facts by age or guarantee that remembered claims remain true.

The starter's system/memory/ folders are instruction and skill scaffolding. They are separate from the app's reviewed memory/<id>.md records. A folder name or a skill's presence does not prove that any particular memory was loaded into the running session.

Use Context window and loadout to inspect what Claude Code reported, and attach the source you want the agent to use. See Keep and recover work for the guide's overview of the available copies.

A review loop for the next turn

  1. Inspect the source. Open the current files and state the goal for the next turn.
  2. Choose the context. Attach relevant passages and inspect the last reported context.
  3. Review the result. Resolve changed excerpts and review the outcome before relying on it.
  4. Update the knowledge. Correct or retire an outdated memory through the available review controls. Restate current requirements or start a new conversation when needed.

These are deliberate review steps. The app's freshness checks do not establish whether an unchanged source is factually correct.

Agent aging: research and coverage

In Your Agents Are Aging Too: Agent Lifespan Engineering for Deployed Systems, Zhu et al. (2026) study reliability as an agent's memory and operating state evolve. Their AgingBench framework distinguishes four failure mechanisms:

Aging mechanismRelated controlsWhat these controls do not establish
Compression: useful details are lost during summarizationLast-reported context and compaction visibility; explicit source selectionThat a summary retained every detail a later task will need
Interference: similar memories obstruct the intended factExact workspace/ref identity and deliberately selected passagesReliable memory retrieval as similar records accumulate
Revision: changes do not propagate correctlyPassage/revision checks and explicit memory correction and retirementCurrent factual truth or automatic updates to dependent claims
Maintenance: lifecycle changes introduce regressionsRecovery controls and the option to start a fresh conversationPreserved knowledge after every compaction or other lifecycle event

This table maps VIKI Agent's controls to related risks. It is not a benchmark result, and these controls do not establish prevention of agent aging.

09A coding workflow you can repeat

The steps below show how you might work on a coding goal in your own project. For example, suppose you want to fix a settings panel that loses a draft when the user changes tabs.

  1. Open and inspect the project. Register the code folder, review the trust information and select it as the session's folder. Its instructions and commands deserve the same review as a project opened directly in Claude Code.
  2. Define a result. Ask the agent to preserve a draft across tab changes, explain the cause and run the project's existing checks. Name the files or behavior that should stay outside the task.
  3. Provide the evidence. Add relevant note excerpts or images and inspect the selected folder context. Reattach an excerpt if its source changes.
  4. Follow the work. Read the plan and tool activity, answer questions and review requested permissions in context. Inspect agent-run results before using them as the basis for a change.
  5. Review the result. Read the changed files and diff. The Code view can commit selected files, review a worktree and run saved checks. A displayed check result does not make other checks unnecessary or establish that the whole change is correct.
  6. Keep what will help later. Record the cause, the decision and the evidence in a note, or prepare a proposal for a protected vault. Use the save or proposal flow that fits the vault's policy.

To let VIKI start a chat for an eligible due task, review What VIKI may do in Decision:

  • Starts
    its grants, activity limits, Pause automatic starts at Claude plan usage and the vault's policy govern those starts.
  • Tool actions
    Claude Code's own permissions still govern them.

Review the chat's conversation and affected files before keeping its result. On every platform, use the controls that platform supports; see Workspaces, notes and code.

10Make repeated work deliberate

A routine saves a prompt, profile, workspace and schedule so that an agreed job can be repeated. A useful first routine might inspect a project's open tasks and draft a weekly review without changing files. Work through it in this order:

  1. Preview its rehearsal.
  2. Run a test.
  3. Inspect the resulting session.
  4. Enable the schedule if the result fits your intent.

Important

Asking for a read-only review in the prompt does not itself restrict the available tools. Choose Claude Code permissions that fit the job.

New scheduled routine runs need VIKI Agent running with an open app window and an awake host.

  • Missed schedule times
    are recorded rather than replayed as a burst of work.
  • Failures
    a failure does not trigger an automatic second attempt. Review the run's result, resolve outstanding permissions or errors and choose Run now when another attempt is appropriate.
  • Decision
    can surface the next routine; it does not create or enable that routine for you.

See Create and run routines for rehearsal, scheduling, pause, history and notification behavior.

A routine can also wait for work and stop short of acting:

  • Only when a card is waiting
    with this setting, a daily or weekly routine skips a scheduled time when no todo card in its vault's kanban/ folder is tagged for its seat. The time is recorded as Skipped and no chat starts.
  • Stop at a draft
    with this setting, a run's permission and plan requests are denied at once, so Claude finishes with a draft. A run that then completes is recorded as Stopped for your decision.

With Start Bots' work in What VIKI may do, VIKI can also start such a routine when one of your cards waits for its seat. See A team using Kanban.

A Bot gives repeated work a place to return to

A Bot links an agent profile and a persistent vault workspace to one reopenable conversation and the routines owned by that pair. It provides a place to check:

  • the current conversation;
  • routine outcomes;
  • optional Mattermost delivery state.

Each routine run still has its own conversation. A delivered notice and a successful local run are separate outcomes.

Continuity also needs review:

  • Saved history can include material that has left the model's active context.
  • A Bot's profile instructions are part of Claude Code's system prompt, which compaction does not summarize. An Agents › Profiles chat's instructions are first-turn text, which compaction can drop.

Check Context & loadout, restate current requirements and choose New conversation when a fresh context is appropriate. A new conversation preserves the previous conversation's history; it does not certify that old assumptions are still true.

See Bots for setup and controls.

11For contributors: trace the workflow

The user-facing concepts above map to these entry points in the source checkout:

Follow this behaviorFile and symbol
Chief's role, specialist roles and the initial instructionsfrontend/src/components/Profiles/seatStarters.ts, SEAT_STARTERS
Active project notes becoming goal titlessrc/viki_agent/automation/brief.py, read_goals; src/viki_agent/decision_loop/state.py, build_state
JEV request and structured response validationsrc/viki_agent/decision_loop/model.py, DecisionModel.ask; the guide and questions in playbook.py
Assessments becoming attention, timing and work choicessrc/viki_agent/decision_loop/arbiter.py, decide; item text in templates.py, render
A Kanban card becoming a Bot runsrc/viki_agent/decision_loop/engine.py, DecisionLoopEngine._plan_seats and _start_seats; seats.py, plan; src/viki_agent/automation/tasks.py, TaskRunner.run_decision

The model-assessment path and the seat-start path are distinct in the engine. When changing proactive behavior, trace the applicable start path as well as its launcher item. Changing a rating does not by itself change routine eligibility, workspace policy or tool permission.
